subject: Closure trajectory stabilization + mop-up plan (MAP update & risk ledger)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0500
Subject: Closure trajectory stabilization + initial risk ledger

Team —

Quick note: Acme reiterated the target close of 2026-12-03 yesterday but flagged two procurement blockers that will likely push the date out if we don’t act: SOC2 evidence and a final procurement sign-off window (they only meet with procurement on Tuesdays). I captured a short risk ledger attached and sketched a proposed MAP update with a conservative rebaseline.

Ask: please review the attached ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx and the risk ledger (close_risk_ledger_20261118.pdf) by EOD Friday. I think we can buy 7–10 days with a partial delivery/canary approach, but that requires an exec call with Acme and an approved exception for a split delivery from our side.

Key mitigation ideas (high level):
- Ship a constrained canary (V1) to validate integrations and unblock their QA — reduces their internal testing backlog.
- Provide SOC2 index and an onsite/recorded walkthrough of controls this week.
- Offer a short-term credit for delayed SLAs if we miss the committed date.

I’ll coordinate the exec call — can Marissa prepare a one-pager on canary scope and Jonas, can you confirm whether procurement can approve a time-limited partial-delivery exception?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP draft — milestones + owners), close_risk_ledger_20261118.pdf (risk heatmap)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Closure trajectory stabilization + initial risk ledger

Thanks Naomi — reviewed and annotated. Attached is a condensed MAP (sheet: ExecutiveSummary) with a two-track milestone path:

Track A (target): full deployment & production sign-off by 2026-12-03 — depends on procurement slot + SOC2 evidence acceptance.
Track B (stabilize): canary delivery to a single integration point + acceptance testing by 2026-11-30 — intended to validate end-to-end flows and remove the largest QA unknowns.

Notes for Jonas: procurement needs the SOC2 evidence index before they can move to legal redlines; I highlighted the specific artifacts in SOC2-evidence-index.docx. If procurement can accept a walkthrough in lieu of full artifact delivery, Track A stays viable.

Action items I’m taking:
- Prepare canary scope (1 page) and test checklist — due Fri 11/20.
- Draft the proposed customer credit language for delayed SLA (optional) — due Mon 11/22.

Connor — can you run a quick feasibility check with infra team on enabling a targeted canary by 11/29 (estimated 48–72h effort)? If that’s a hard no, we need to pivot.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx (annotated), SOC2-evidence-index.docx

From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Acme Solutions Ops <solutions@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Closure trajectory stabilization + initial risk ledger

Naomi / Marissa — appreciate the quick follow-up and the draft MAP. Two points from procurement and our security review that will materially affect the timeline: 

1) SOC2 evidence: procurement requires the SOC2 artifact set (description of controls + test evidence samples). A walkthrough is helpful but not a replacement for the evidence collection step — our legal/procurement will need to attach artifacts to the contract. That adds a dependency we didn’t estimate earlier.

2) Procurement cadence: our procurement team runs formal signings Tuesdays and policy reviews Fridays. The earliest formal approval window with artifacts attached would be Tue 2026-12-07.

We’re open to the canary idea for earlier validation, but we cannot sign for full production until procurement attaches the artifact set. If Redwood can provide the evidence index and a recorded controls walkthrough by EOD Friday 11/20, we’ll prioritize a special review but can’t promise earlier than 12/07 for contract signature.

I’ll coordinate internally and loop back with a firm date once procurement confirms whether a Friday ad-hoc review is possible.

Regards,
Sarah Park
Director, Solutions — Acme Corporation

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Closure trajectory stabilization + initial risk ledger

Sarah — thanks for the clarity. Understood on procurement windows. We can commit to the following immediately: 

- Deliver a SOC2 evidence index + recorded walkthrough by EOD Friday 11/20 (SOC2-evidence-index.docx) — Marissa is finalizing the narrative and Connor will record the controls walkthrough with our security engineer.
- Prepare a scoped canary plan that pulls no contractual dependencies: limited feature set, single integration endpoint, rollback plan — will be ready by Fri 11/20 COB.
- If Acme agrees to the canary, Redwood will offer a 10% service credit applied to the first month of invoicing if the final production start slips past 2026-12-03. This is a temporary concession to preserve the commercial posture while we de-risk the path to production.

We’d like to set a short exec sync (30 minutes) next week to align on the canary acceptance criteria and procurement expectations. Proposed slots: Mon 11/23 10:00–10:30am ET or Tue 11/24 2:00–2:30pm ET.

If procurement confirms an ad-hoc Friday review, that could keep Track A alive; otherwise Track B (canary-first) becomes the safe path.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-index.docx (to follow), ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx (tracked changes)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: VP Revenue <vp_revenue@redwood.com>, CRO <cro@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0500
Subject: Escalation: Acme close - procurement cadence creating slip risk (ask: exec sponsor for canary & credit approval)

Hi — quick escalation summary and ask. 

Deal: Acme Corporation (ACME-2201)
Current committed close: 2026-12-03
Risk: Procurement policy + SOC2 artifact requirement push earliest signing to 2026-12-07 -> 4-day slippage risk to committed close. Additional internal QA unknowns increase effective risk window to ~10 days.

Mitigation proposal (seeking exec direction/approval):
- Approve a canary-first delivery (Track B) to validate integrations by 2026-11-30. This requires a short-term exception to our standard production-only launch policy.
- Approve a 10% one-time service credit if final production start slips beyond 2026-12-03.
- Assign an exec sponsor to join a 30-minute alignment call with Acme next week to unblock procurement.

Attachments: close_risk_ledger_20261118.pdf (detailed heatmap), ACME_MAP_v2.xlsx (proposed two-track plan)

Why this is recommended: a canary reduces the largest failure modes before full sign-off and preserves trust with Acme; the credit buys us goodwill without material revenue impact given contract size.

Ask: Can VP Revenue or CRO approve the above by EOD today so we can propose the exec slot to Acme?

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
